memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: You have been rebellious against the Lord ever since I have known you. I lay prostrate before the Lord those forty days and forty nights because the Lord had said he would destroy you. I prayed to the Lord and said, "Sovereign Lord, do not destroy your people, your own inheritance that you redeemed by your great power and brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand." - Deut 9:24-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here we hear the words of Moses' prayer itself, and they are worth savouring. Notice what he appeals to. He does not argue that the people deserve to be spared — he has just admitted they have been rebellious all along. Instead, he appeals to God's own investment in them: "your people, your own inheritance that you redeemed... and brought out of Egypt." Moses grounds his plea not in Israel's worthiness but in God's character, God's purposes, and what God has already done for them.

This is the secret of confident prayer. When we come to God, we do not come pleading our own goodness or the goodness of those we pray for — that ground is always shaky. We come appealing to who God is: His mercy, His faithfulness, His redeeming love, His commitment to His own people. Moses essentially prays, "These are Yours, Lord. You redeemed them. Remember Your own work." That is a prayer that moves the heart of God.

We can pray the same way. When we or those we love have failed, we do not appeal to our track record but to God's grace and His finished work in Christ. We belong to Him; He redeemed us at the cost of His Son's blood. When we plead, "Lord, I am Yours, bought by Christ," we stand on the firmest ground there is. Moses' prayer teaches us to anchor our confidence not in ourselves but in the redeeming God who does not abandon what He has purchased. Pray boldly today on the basis of who God is and what Christ has done.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- When I pray, do I appeal to my own goodness or to God's character?
- How does grounding prayer in God's redeeming love give me confidence?
- What situation can I bring to God today on the basis of "I am Yours"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Sovereign Lord, I come to You not on the basis of my worthiness but on the basis of who You are and what Christ has done. I am Yours, redeemed by His blood. Remember Your own work in me, and hear my prayer. Amen.
